description: The American Robin is one of the most familiar songbirds across North America, often spotted hopping across lawns in search of food. It is recognized by its warm orange-red breast, grayish-brown back, and distinctive white markings around the eyes. Despite its name, the American robin is not closely related to the European Robin; the name was inspired by a superficial resemblance noticed by early settlers. Widespread and adaptable, American robins inhabit forests, gardens, parks, and suburban areas, thriving in close proximity to human activity. Their diet shifts with the seasons—earthworms and insects are staples in spring and summer, while fruits and berries become more important in fall and winter. Known for their clear, melodious song, robins are often among the first birds to sing at dawn and are widely regarded as a harbinger of spring.
title: American Robin in Golden Gate Park

description: The white stork, seen here soaring in the peaceful blue skies of Ukraine, is a large migratory wading bird known for its long legs, long red bill, and broad wings. It often soars on thermal currents with its neck outstretched and is widely seen across Europe and parts of Asia and Africa. This bird is closely associated with open wetlands, grasslands, and farmland, where it forages for insects, frogs, and small reptiles.
title: White Stork in the blue sky of Ukraine

description: Calandrinia grandiflora, commonly known as rock purslane, is a species of flowering plant in the Portulacaceae family. It is native to the western United States and is commonly found in rocky areas, such as cliffs and rocky hillsides. The plant has small, bright yellow flowers and is often used in landscaping and as a ground cover due to its low maintenance requirements and ability to thrive in difficult conditions.
title: Calandrinia grandiflora (Rock purslane)

description: The vivid blooms of Pelargonium × hortorum, commonly known as garden geraniums, stand out in this close-up composition. Widely cultivated as ornamental plants, zonal geraniums are prized for their dense flower heads and long blooming season. Native to Southern Africa through their parent species, these plants thrive in sunny conditions and are a common feature in gardens and window boxes, where their bold colors and resilience make them especially popular.
title: Zonal geranium (or garden geranium)

description: Tropaeolum, commonly known as nasturtium, is a genus of flowering plants native to parts of Central and South America. These plants are widely grown as ornamentals and are especially valued for their vivid blossoms, rounded leaves, and easy-growing nature in gardens and containers. Many species and cultivated varieties belong to the family Tropaeolaceae, a small plant family best known for nasturtiums themselves. Nasturtiums are also notable for being edible: their leaves, flowers, and immature seeds have a peppery flavor that has made them a familiar ingredient in salads and garnishes. Popular in horticulture since at least the early modern period, they attract pollinators such as bees and hummingbirds in suitable regions. With their blend of ornamental appeal and culinary usefulness, nasturtiums remain a favorite in both decorative and practical planting.
title: Tropaeolum, commonly known as nasturtium

description: The term “pine forest” refers to woodland dominated by trees in the genus Pinus, one of the largest groups of conifers on Earth. Pine species grow across much of the Northern Hemisphere and are well adapted to a wide range of environments, from cool mountain slopes to sandy lowlands. Their needle-like leaves help reduce water loss, and their seeds develop in the familiar cones associated with conifer trees. Pine forests play an important ecological role by providing habitat for birds, mammals, insects, and fungi, while also helping stabilize soil and store carbon. Many species are valued in forestry for timber, paper production, and resin, and pine woodlands have long been associated with hiking, recreation, and protected natural landscapes. Their evergreen character gives them a distinct presence through the seasons, even in regions with cold winters.
title: Pine Forest

description: Hoar frost forms when water vapor in the air freezes directly onto cold surfaces, creating delicate white ice crystals that can coat twigs, branches, and other exposed objects. Unlike ordinary frozen dew, it develops through deposition rather than from liquid water first collecting and then freezing, and it is most likely to appear in calm, humid conditions when temperatures remain below freezing. In many temperate regions, leafless trees are a familiar part of winter. Deciduous species shed their leaves in autumn as part of a seasonal cycle that helps conserve water and energy during colder months. When frost settles across bare branches, it can briefly transform an ordinary woodland scene into a striking display of pattern, texture, and winter light.
title: Trees with branches covered in hoar-frost
